## Trigger

When harness work consumes hours and excessive inference, I want the complete audit and recommendations preserved in the tracker, so I can approve focused changes that reduce time and token waste.

## Findings and reasons

Repeated verification, compulsory tracker ceremony, broad context priming, conflicting repair and validation roles, consumer prompts referencing authoring-only scripts, whole-batch completion barriers, findings delivered only at redispatch, cleanup after closure and late confirmation are established mechanisms. Tracker UI polling adds repeated requests. Historical full verification took 185.826 seconds including pytest 138.127 seconds. A fresh ranking profile took 0.861 seconds wall and 0.806 seconds process CPU; this does not establish sustained saturation or hours-scale effects across consumer repositories.

## Durable evidence

The audit-report artifact contains every recommendation and reason, evidence citations, all 26 skill dispositions, 307 file dispositions and the conceptual dependency map. The audit-evidence artifact contains the tracked inventory, resolved dependencies and independent kit/web reviews. Static dependency references do not prove runtime reachability. Existing performance program basicly-c25o52c remains distinct.

## Approval boundary

User authorized this audit, tracker persistence and next-release planning on 2026-10-17. Filing a story is not implementation approval. All recommendations require individual review and approval. Do not claim, dispatch, implement, cut a release or change policy from this outline. Existing records, requirements, ownership and pre-existing ledger work must remain intact.

## Trigger

When routine harness work spends excessive time on process, context and repeated checks, I want the next release to remove the largest avoidable costs first, so later implementation runs with less time and inference waste.

## Recommended release

Proposed v0.26.0: focused delivery with less ceremony and repeated verification. This is a planning recommendation, not a version bump, approved implementation or release authorization. It uses stories from the complete audit basicly-h79lott and retains the broader performance program basicly-c25o52c.

## Priority and sequence

1. Record representative workflow baselines and review concrete time/token budgets before optimization.
2. Reduce task-expanding instructions, compulsory broad priming and small-task tracker ceremony.
3. Repair authoring-only instructions in consumer paths and the two known landing/cleanup lifecycle defects.
4. Remove measured equivalent verification and validation/review work while preserving input identity and safety.
5. Prove the exact candidate with the same workloads and a clean consumer upgrade.

## Explicit exclusions

Defer batch-streaming orchestration, running-lane notifications, new skill profile machinery, general resource scheduling, broad scan/index optimization, tracker UI redesign and optional comment/style/dead-code policy retirements. Do not combine these into the first release merely because they appear in the audit. Existing Pyright caching, affected-check providers, fail-fast and Codex workspace profiles already exist; enabling them again is not delivery.

## Approval and release policy

Every selected recommendation requires individual user approval and implementation refinement. A sequence is not a dispatch grant. If a selected item cannot be bounded without a large framework or unrelated refactor, return its concrete tradeoff for review rather than expanding the release. Release acceptance uses observed results, not predicted speedups. No arbitrary numeric improvement is claimed before the baseline is reviewed.

basicly-ewepxov.description:
## Trigger

When a verified task produces normal tool artifacts, I want to finish shipping without manual cache moves, so I can return to feature work while unrelated files and failed cleanup remain recoverable.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run normal full verification and prepare pinned build artifacts in a harness task worktree.
2. Approve ship and resume the loop. Cleanup refuses project bytecode, pytest, Ruff, import-linter cache and verified build outputs.
3. Observe that the current ship implementation has already closed the record before cleanup raises. A repeat loop run reports already shipped and leaves the worktree behind.
4. A driver currently has to preserve about twenty generated paths manually, invoke worktree cleanup separately, and commit remaining tracker state. The progress task basicly-8vy4 reproduced this exact failure; later tasks used manual preservation before ship to avoid it.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/worktree.py`
- `src/basicly/worktree_contents.py`
- `src/basicly/loop.py`
- `tests/test_worktree.py`
- `tests/test_worktree_contents.py`
- `tests/test_worktree_safety.py`
- `tests/test_loop.py`
- `tests/test_integration_loop.py`
- `changelog.d/*.md`

## Design

Keep artifact ownership strict and evidence based. Derive known generated-artifact recognition from the actual producers and pinned build manifest, preserving unknown content, symlinks, tracked changes and all existing checkout identity/lock/unmerged guards. Prefer reversible preservation when ownership does not justify discarding an artifact; never treat every ignored path as disposable. Centralize behavior so ordinary worktree cleanup and loop ship share it. A failed cleanup must leave an open, retryable record; actual criterion confirmation still precedes teardown. Keep completion refusals recoverable and repeated attempts idempotent. Do not touch other sessions or historical worktrees, require force, change permissions, add dependencies or bypass hooks.

## Demonstration

Install the candidate into a disposable consumer, run verification that creates the supported actual tool artifacts, land normally, and ship using ordinary loop commands with no manual cache relocation. Exercise foreign and malformed cache files, symlinks and a cleanup failure: they must preserve data and the open record. Remove only the fixture-owned blocker and retry; assert one clean closure and no live worktree. Keep actual argv, outputs, archive/preservation locations where applicable and elapsed command time in the proof.

## Trigger

When a lane lands without recorded confirmation evidence, I want the landing refused before the merge, so I can keep main and the record in step.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Drive a bead to build with no cli.py confirm recorded.
2. loop run with the manual runner merges and rebases the branch into main, then prints only [blocked] build -> build: confirmation lacks actual successful check evidence.
3. loop status reports phase build with the worktree still present, and an unattributed tracker event is left uncommitted in base. In code, src/basicly/loop.py _verify_and_land calls merge.merge_worktree before _record_verify reaches process_confirmation.confirm.

Found 2026-10-07 while walking docs/tutorial/first-loop.md against the v0.21.0 candidate.
